Dear Rainbow Six Siege,

From the very first time I loaded into a match, I knew there was something different about you. At first, I thought you were just another tactical shooter, another game to play for a few hours and move on from. I could not have been more wrong. What started as curiosity slowly became admiration, and before I knew it, it became something much deeper: genuine love.

There is something magical about the way every round feels important. Every footstep, every drone, every barricade, every heartbeat in the final seconds of a 1v1 situation matters. You taught me that victory is not just about having the best aim. It's about patience, strategy, teamwork, communication, adaptation, and keeping a cool head when everything is falling apart. Few games have ever made me think as much as you have, and even fewer have made me feel the rush that comes from pulling off the impossible.

I love your destruction system. I love how walls are never just walls. Floors are never just floors. Ceilings are never just ceilings. Every surface is an opportunity, a threat, a possibility. Every map feels alive because no two rounds are ever the same. The battlefield constantly changes, and with it, the stories that unfold. One moment I'm carefully droning a room, and the next I'm rappelling upside down outside a window wondering whether I'm about to make the greatest play of my life or the dumbest mistake imaginable.

I love your operators. Every one of them brings something unique to the table. Whether I'm breaching reinforced walls, gathering intel, setting traps, healing teammates, or anchoring a site against overwhelming odds, there is always a role to play and a way to contribute. The variety keeps every match fresh, and learning how different operators interact with one another feels like studying an endless game of chess where the pieces can suddenly blow holes through the board.

I love the tension you create. Few experiences in gaming compare to being the last player alive with the clock ticking down, teammates watching, and the entire outcome resting on your shoulders. My heart races, my hands sweat, and for those brief moments, nothing else matters. Win or lose, those moments stay with me long after the match is over.

Of course, our relationship hasn't always been perfect. You've frustrated me. You've tested my patience. You've introduced operators I didn't understand, maps I got lost on, and opponents who somehow knew exactly where I was at all times. There were moments when I swore I needed a break from you. Yet somehow, after all the frustration, I always found myself coming back. Not because I had to, but because no other game gave me the same feeling.

You've given me unforgettable memories with friends. Countless laughs. Clutch victories. Catastrophic failures that became inside jokes. Hours spent planning strategies that immediately fell apart. Celebrations after impossible comebacks. Moments of pure chaos that somehow turned into triumph. Those memories are worth more than any rank or statistic.

What I admire most is your depth. Even after hundreds or thousands of hours, there is always something new to learn. A new angle. A new strategy. A new way to approach a site. A better way to communicate with teammates. The journey of improvement never truly ends, and that is part of what makes you so special.

Rainbow Six Siege, you are more than just a game to me. You are a challenge, a hobby, a source of excitement, frustration, joy, and accomplishment. You have kept me engaged for years in a way that very few games ever could. Every match tells a story, every victory feels earned, and every defeat is a lesson waiting to be learned.

Thank you for the unforgettable moments, the adrenaline-filled clutches, the friendships forged through teamwork, and the countless hours of entertainment. No matter how many games come and go, there will always be something special about returning to you.

With love,

A devoted Siege player

Ich starte Rainbow Six Siege.

Dokkaebi.

Nächste Runde.

Dokkaebi.

NOCH EINE RUNDE.

Dokkaebi.

Sie ist gefühlt in jeder verdammten Runde dabei und einfach viel zu stark geworden. Egal welche Seite, egal welche Map, irgendwo läuft immer eine Dokkaebi herum und nervt die komplette Lobby.

Dann kommt noch diese neue Map dazu. Wer auch immer auf die Idee gekommen ist, eine Map so riesig zu machen, hat komplett den Verstand verloren. Ich verbringe mehr Zeit damit herumzulaufen als tatsächlich Gegner zu suchen. Bis ich ankomme, ist die halbe Runde schon vorbei.

Und natürlich gibt es noch die Peeker. Der Gegner sieht mich gefühlt drei Jahre früher als ich ihn. Auf meinem Bildschirm sehe ich einen einzelnen Pixel und im nächsten Moment liege ich schon auf dem Boden. Absolut lächerlich.

Die Teammates machen die Sache auch nicht besser. Der eine stirbt direkt nach dem Spawn, der nächste ignoriert jede Information und der dritte spielt wahrscheinlich mit ausgeschaltetem Monitor.

Jede Runde sorgt für neue Aggressionen. Man regt sich über denselben Mist auf, dieselben Operatoren, dieselben Peeker und dieselben bescheuerten Situationen. Dieses Spiel schafft es immer wieder, mich komplett ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ und mir mentale Schäden zu verpassen.

Wer behauptet, Rainbow Six Siege sei entspannend, hat dieses verdammte Spiel noch nie gespielt.
